examples.en: The tiger is looking for prey.

examples.ko: 사냥꾼은 오늘 아무 사냥감도 못 잡았어요.
examples.en: The hunter caught no game today.
Lions go after weak prey first.
In winter the prey becomes scarce, so animals have a hard time.

examples.ko: 그 새는 작은 곤충을 사냥감으로 삼아요.
examples.en: That bird takes small insects as its prey.

examples.ko: 잡은 사냥감을 마을 사람들과 나눠 먹었어요.
examples.en: They shared the game they caught with the villagers.

explain: '사냥감'은 사냥해서 잡는 동물이고, 먹잇감으로 쓰는 말은 '먹이'예요. 동물을 말할 때는 '먹이'를 더 많이 쓰고, 사냥하는 사람이 있을 때는 '사냥감'이 어울려요. 짝말은 '사냥꾼'이에요.

phrases.en: The dog chased its prey and ran into the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사냥감을 뒤따라 달릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when running after prey.

phrases.en: The eagle is eyeing its prey from the sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡으려고 겨냥하고 있을 때 써요. 사람을 목표로 말할 때 비유로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when aiming to catch something. It can also be a metaphor for targeting a person.

phrases.en: The lion is looking for food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이 먹는 것을 넓게 말해요. 사냥하는 사람이 없는 경우에 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word for what animals eat. More common when no hunter is involved.

explain_en: '사냥감' is an animal that is hunted. For animals eating in general, '먹이' (food) is more common, while '사냥감' fits when a hunter is involved. Its partner word is '사냥꾼', the hunter.

t90.ax: The tiger is looking for prey.

examples.en: This piano sheet music is too difficult.
I practice a song while looking at the sheet music.
You can buy sheet music at a bookstore.
I marked the score with a pencil.
I'm a beginner who can't even read sheet music.

examples.ko: 악보의 첫 줄이 이해가 안 돼요.
examples.en: I don't understand the first line of the score.

explain: '악보를 보다', '악보를 읽다'처럼 써요. 책으로 묶은 것은 '악보집'이라고 해요. 노래 가사만 적은 종이는 악보가 아니라 '가사'예요.

phrases.en: I play guitar while looking at the sheet music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악보를 눈으로 보며 연주할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when playing while looking at the music.

phrases.example: 저는 아직 악보를 잘 못 읽어요.
phrases.en: I still can't read sheet music well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음표를 이해하는 능력을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the ability to understand the notes.

phrases.en: I bought a piano music book at the bookstore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악보를 책으로 묶은 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A book that collects sheet music.

explain_en: It is used as '악보를 보다' or '악보를 읽다'. A bound collection is a '악보집'. A sheet with only the lyrics is '가사', not '악보'.

examples.en: I check my daily horoscope every morning.

examples.ko: 새해에는 한 해 운세를 보러 가는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people go to have their fortune for the year read at New Year.
I heard that my fortune is good this year.
My friend checked my fortune using an app.

examples.ko: 운세에 너무 매달리지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to rely too much on fortune telling.

examples.ko: 신문 맨 뒤에는 띠별 운세가 실려 있어요.
examples.en: The zodiac fortunes are printed on the back page of the newspaper.

explain: '운세'는 한 해, 한 달, 하루의 운이 어떻게 흘러갈지를 점쳐서 보는 것을 말할 때 써요. 그날그날 일이 풀리는 정도를 말하는 '운수'와 달리 '운세를 보다/풀이하다'로 점과 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 띠나 별자리별 운세를 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: I had my fortune read together with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점을 쳐서 운이 어떤지 알아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking one's luck through fortune-telling.

phrases.en: I read the fortune by zodiac animal in the newspaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 태어난 해의 띠에 따른 운세를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fortune based on the zodiac animal of one's birth year.

phrases.en: They say this year's fortune is very good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 해의 운을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for one's luck over the year.

explain_en: 운세 is used for reading how your luck will go over a year, a month or a day. Unlike 운수, the luck of the moment, it is often used together with fortune-telling, as in '운세를 보다/풀이하다'. People often check the 운세 for their zodiac animal or star sign.

t90.ax: I check my daily horoscope every morning.

examples.en: Today is the solar term when autumn begins.
Korea has twenty-four solar terms.
Grandmother cooks food to match the solar terms.

examples.ko: 동지는 일 년 중 밤이 가장 긴 절기예요.
examples.en: Dongji is the solar term with the longest night of the year.

examples.ko: 절기를 알면 날씨 변화를 미리 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you know the solar terms, you can anticipate weather changes.
By the solar calendar it's spring, but it is still cold.

explain: '절기'는 한 해를 24개로 나눈 옛 달력의 계절 구분이에요. 입춘, 하지, 동지처럼 날씨와 농사에 쓰였어요. 요즘도 '절기상으로는 봄인데'처럼 날씨 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: By the solar calendar, it is already winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨 이야기에서 달력상의 계절을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in weather talk for the calendar season.

phrases.en: Ipchun is one of the twenty-four solar terms.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 해를 나눈 절기의 전체 수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the full set of terms dividing the year.

phrases.en: The food people eat is different for each solar term.
phrases.nuance_ko: 절기와 생활 습관을 연결할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to connect the solar terms with daily customs.

explain_en: 절기 is the old calendar's way of dividing the year into 24 seasonal points, such as 입춘, 하지 and 동지, used for weather and farming. Today you still hear it in weather talk, like 절기상으로는 봄인데.

examples.ko: 할머니는 요즘 동작이 굼떠서 계단이 힘드세요.
examples.en: Grandmother's movements have gotten slow lately, so stairs are hard for her.
If you move that sluggishly, you'll be late.
In the morning, both my mind and body are sluggish.

examples.ko: 행동이 굼뜬 사람은 급한 일에 불리해요.
examples.en: A person who acts slowly is at a disadvantage in urgent situations.

examples.ko: 일 처리가 굼뜨니 손님이 기다리다 가셨어요.
examples.en: Because the work was handled so slowly, the customer waited and then left.
Please don't tease me for being slow, and just wait for me.

explain: '느리다'는 속도가 느린 것이고, 굼뜨다는 사람의 몸이나 행동이 둔하고 답답하게 느릴 때 써서 조금 부정적이에요. 반대말로는 '재빠르다', '날쌔다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: Because of my sluggish movements, I'm always late.
phrases.nuance_ko: '굼뜬'이 명사 '동작'을 꾸미는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form 굼뜬 describing the noun 동작.

phrases.en: In the morning my body feels sluggish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 자기 몸의 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form for describing one's own sluggish state.

phrases.en: Grandfather isn't slow even though he's old.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 동작이 빠릿하다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative, it means someone is quick and sharp.

explain_en: '느리다' simply means slow, while 굼뜨다 describes a person's body or actions as dull and frustratingly slow, so it sounds a bit negative. Its opposites include '재빠르다' and '날쌔다'.

t90.ax: If you move that sluggishly, you'll be late.

examples.en: The baby looked at me and smiled.
Grandma smiled and waved her hand.

examples.ko: 그 일에 대해서는 아무도 입을 벙긋도 안 했어요.
examples.en: Nobody breathed a word about that matter.
When the photographer spoke, everyone smiled.

examples.ko: 선생님은 아이를 보며 벙긋 웃어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher looked at the child and gave a smile.

examples.ko: 친구가 그 얘기를 듣고 벙긋 미소를 지었어요.
examples.en: My friend heard the story and broke into a smile.

explain: 소리 없이 입을 살짝 벌려 웃는 모습이에요. 웃음뿐 아니라 '입을 벙긋도 안 하다'처럼 입을 열어 말하려는 동작에도 써요. 이 경우는 거의 부정형으로 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 일에 대해서는 아무도 입도 벙긋 안 했어요.
phrases.en: Nobody said a word about that matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말을 한마디도 하지 않는다는 굳은 표현이에요. 주로 부정형으로 쓰고, 비밀이나 침묵을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set expression meaning not saying a single word. It is used mostly in the negative and fits secrets or silence.

explain_en: It shows a silent smile with the mouth opening slightly. Besides smiles, it is also used for the motion of opening the mouth to speak, as in '입을 벙긋도 안 하다'. In that sense it is almost always used in the negative.

t90.ax: The baby looked at me and smiled.

examples.ko: 알람이 아침 일곱 시로 설정돼 있어요.
examples.en: The alarm is set for seven in the morning.
A new password has been set.
If the goal is set too high, it's hard.
After the set time passes, the screen turns off.
The language is set to Korean.
The price is expected to be set low.

explain: 휴대폰·프로그램의 '설정'은 값을 정해 두는 일이고, '설정되다'는 이미 그렇게 정해진 상태예요. 목표·기준에도 써요. 말로는 '맞춰져 있다'가 더 자연스럽고, 직접 바꿀 때는 '설정하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The clock is set to the exact time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말로는 '설정되다'보다 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural in speech than 설정되다.

phrases.en: The screen brightness is set automatically.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자동으로'와 함께 기계나 앱에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with '자동으로' for devices and apps.

phrases.en: I set an alarm on my phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 직접 정할 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, when a person sets it directly.

explain_en: For phones and programs, '설정' is fixing a value; '설정되다' means it is already set. It also works for goals and standards. In speech, '맞춰져 있다' is more natural; when you change it yourself, use '설정하다'.

t90.ax: A new password has been set.

en: to eradicate; to wipe out; to eliminate

examples.ko: 약을 뿌려서 집 안의 벌레를 퇴치했어요.
examples.en: I sprayed insecticide and got rid of the bugs in the house.
To eradicate this disease, a vaccine is needed.
Farmers research ways to get rid of pests.

examples.ko: 모기를 퇴치할 수 있는 식물이 있대요.
examples.en: They say there are plants that can repel mosquitoes.
The village became quiet after getting rid of the rats.
It took a long time to completely wipe out the epidemic.

explain: '없애다'는 뭐든 쓸 수 있지만 '퇴치하다'는 벌레, 병, 해로운 풀처럼 해로운 대상에 써요. '짐을 퇴치하다'처럼 말하면 어색해요. 어려운 대상일수록 '완전히 퇴치하다'처럼 자주 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I sprayed medicine and got rid of the mosquitoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해로운 벌레를 없앨 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for getting rid of harmful bugs.

phrases.example: 의사들은 그 병을 완전히 퇴치하고 싶어 해요.
phrases.en: Doctors want to completely wipe out that disease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하나도 남기지 않고 없앤다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the sense of removing it without leaving any.

phrases.example: 집 안의 바퀴벌레를 빨리 퇴치해야 해요.
phrases.en: We have to get rid of the cockroaches in the house quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 없애야 하는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something must be eliminated.

explain_en: '없애다' can be used for anything, but 퇴치하다 is for harmful targets such as insects, diseases and harmful weeds. Saying '짐을 퇴치하다' (get rid of luggage) sounds odd. For hard targets it often appears as '완전히 퇴치하다'.

t90.ax: Farmers research ways to get rid of pests.

en: to be used; to be utilized

examples.en: This app is used in class.
The leftover ingredients were used in another dish.
AI is being used in many places.

examples.ko: 잘 활용되지 않는 방이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There's a room that isn't put to good use.
The range of uses keeps widening.

examples.ko: 이 자료는 시험 공부에 활용될 거예요.
examples.en: These materials will be used for exam study.

explain: '활용되다'는 가진 것이 쓸모 있게 쓰일 때 써요. 그냥 '쓰이다'보다 잘 살려 쓴다는 느낌이 들어요. '~에 활용되다'로 써요.

phrases.en: This tool is used in many ways.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 가지로 쓰일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something serves many purposes.

phrases.example: 이 기술은 여러 분야에 널리 활용돼요.
phrases.en: This technology is widely used in many fields.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많은 곳에서 쓰일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it's used in many places.

phrases.en: I make good use of my time to study.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person using it is the subject.

explain_en: 활용되다 is used when something one has is put to useful work. Compared with plain 쓰이다, it gives the feel of being used well. It appears as '~에 활용되다'.

gh: used as a means; may imply exploitation

p.n: 활용되다 stresses making the best use of it. 사용되다 just says it is used.

t90.ax: This app is used in class.

examples.en: The army retreated because the enemy was strong.
The economy is declining as business gets worse.

examples.ko: 한 걸음 후퇴해서 다시 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's step back and think again.

examples.ko: 복지 제도가 후퇴하지 않도록 사람들이 목소리를 냈어요.
examples.en: People spoke up so that the welfare system would not slide backward.
I practice every day for fear my skills will slip.

examples.ko: 공격하던 팀이 갑자기 후퇴하는 바람에 골을 먹었어요.
examples.en: The attacking team suddenly fell back and we conceded a goal.

explain: 싸움에서 뒤로 물러날 때 쓰고, 실력이나 경제가 나빠질 때 비유로도 써요. 반대말은 '전진하다'나 '발전하다'예요. 일상에서 그냥 뒤로 가는 건 '물러나다'나 '뒤로 가다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The soldiers slowly stepped back.
phrases.nuance_ko: '후퇴하다'보다 일상에서 더 자연스럽고 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more natural in daily speech than '후퇴하다'.

phrases.en: The commander gave the order to retreat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '후퇴'는 싸움 이야기에서 '명령'과 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun often goes with '명령' in stories about battle.

phrases.en: We moved forward without retreating.
phrases.nuance_ko: '후퇴하다'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '후퇴하다'.

explain_en: It is used when pulling back in a fight, and figuratively when skills or the economy get worse. The opposites are '전진하다' and '발전하다'. For simply moving back in daily life people say '물러나다' or '뒤로 가다'.

dis.h: move back; also fall back in general
gh: retreat of an army, formal military term

p.n: 퇴각하다 is only for armies and is more formal; 후퇴하다 can also describe sports or the economy.

t90.ax: Let's step back and think again.

en: to be absorbed; to be soaked; to be consumed

examples.en: Water is absorbed quickly by a sponge.
Sweat is absorbed well by this clothing.

examples.ko: 크림은 피부에 흡수되는 데 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes time for cream to be absorbed into the skin.

examples.ko: 영양분이 몸에 흡수되려면 잘 씹어야 해요.
examples.en: To have nutrients absorbed by the body, you need to chew well.
The small company was absorbed into the large one.
I feel like the new knowledge has soaked into my head.

explain: 물, 영양분, 소리가 다른 것 안으로 빨려 들어갈 때 써요. 회사나 문화가 큰 쪽에 합쳐질 때도 써요. 주어는 흡수되는 것이고 '에'로 들어가는 곳을 말해요. 하는 쪽은 '흡수하다'예요.

phrases.en: The nutrients in food are absorbed in the intestines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸 안으로 영양분이 들어갈 때 쓰는 대표 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical use for nutrients entering the body.

phrases.en: Sound is absorbed because of the thick curtains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 퍼지지 않고 사라지는 느낌일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when sound doesn't spread and seems to disappear.

phrases.en: The small company was absorbed into the big company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 쪽이 큰 쪽에 합쳐져 사라지는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a smaller body merges into and disappears within a bigger one.
phrases.en_equiv: is absorbed into a big company

explain_en: It is used when water, nutrients, or sound are drawn into something else, and also when a company or culture is merged into a larger one. The subject is what gets absorbed and 에 marks where it goes. The active form is 흡수하다.

examples.ko: 이 차선은 시간대에 따라 가변으로 운영돼요.
examples.en: This lane is operated flexibly depending on the time of day.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 높이가 가변이라서 키에 맞춰 조절해요.
examples.en: The height of this chair is adjustable, so you set it to your height.

examples.ko: 가변 좌석이 있어서 공간을 넓게 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: There are adjustable seats, so you can use the space widely.
The schedule is subject to change, so I'll let you know once it's fixed.

examples.ko: 요금이 가변적으로 바뀌어서 미리 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: The fare changes depending on conditions, so you should check beforehand.
This rule can vary depending on the situation.

explain: 반대말은 '고정'이고, '가변 좌석', '가변 차선'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 일정이나 상황처럼 바뀔 수 있는 것에는 '가변적'이라고도 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '바뀔 수 있는'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 극장의 가변 좌석은 공연에 따라 바꿀 수 있어요.
phrases.en: The theater's flexible seating can be changed depending on the show.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가변'을 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 대표적인 예예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical example of attaching 가변 before a noun.

phrases.en: The schedule can change, so it isn't certain yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가변'보다 서술어로 쓰기 쉬운 형태로, 바뀔 수 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier predicate form meaning 'subject to change'.

phrases.en: A reversible lane operates during rush hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간에 따라 방향이나 쓰임이 바뀌는 도로 차선이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A road lane whose direction or use changes with the time of day.

explain_en: Its opposite is '고정' (fixed), and it is often placed before a noun as in '가변 좌석' or '가변 차선'. For things that may change, like schedules or situations, '가변적' is also used. In casual talk people often say '바뀔 수 있는' instead.

examples.en: People's outfits in the park are all different.
Balloons of every color floated up into the sky.
The students' dreams are all different, which is interesting.
All sorts of reactions came out.
The umbrellas opened in every color.
In autumn, the mountain's leaves are of every color.

explain: 색깔뿐 아니라 모양, 생각, 반응이 각각 다를 때도 써요. '가지가지'는 종류가 많은 걸, '가지각색'은 서로 다르게 다양한 걸 강조해요. '가지각색이다', '가지각색의'처럼 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The colors of the flowers are really varied.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다'를 붙여 '서로 다 다르다'는 뜻으로 문장을 끝낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 이다, it ends a sentence to say that things are all different.

phrases.en: There are all sorts of clothes at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 의, it modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.en: The shop has all kinds of fruit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가지각색'은 서로 다른 것을, '가지가지'는 종류가 많다는 것을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 가지각색 stresses that they differ; 가지가지 stresses that there are many kinds.

explain_en: It covers not only colors but also shapes, opinions and reactions that all differ. '가지가지' stresses many kinds, while '가지각색' stresses that each is different. It is typically said as '가지각색이다' or '가지각색의'.

t90.ax: All sorts of reactions came out.

en: to be strange; to be weird; to be odd

examples.en: I heard a weird sound in the forest and got scared.

examples.ko: 그 건물은 모양이 괴이해서 눈길을 끌어요.
examples.en: That building catches the eye because its shape is so odd.

examples.ko: 괴이하게도 그날 밤 시계가 모두 멈췄어요.
examples.en: Strangely enough, all the clocks stopped that night.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 행동이 너무 괴이해서 다들 피했어요.
examples.en: His behavior was so strange that everyone avoided him.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 분위기가 괴이하지만 자꾸 보게 돼요.
examples.en: The mood of this painting is eerie, but I keep looking at it.

examples.ko: 오래된 집에서 괴이한 일이 계속 생겼대요.
examples.en: I heard strange things kept happening in the old house.

explain: '이상하다'보다 섬뜩하고 기이한 느낌이 있고, 말보다는 글이나 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요. '괴이하게도'처럼 문장 앞에서 놀라운 일을 소개할 때도 써요. 평소 대화에서는 '이상하다'나 '수상하다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Strange things kept happening in the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설명하기 어려운 섬뜩한 사건을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for creepy events that are hard to explain.

phrases.example: 괴이하게도 아무도 그 방에 들어가지 못했어요.
phrases.en: Strangely enough, no one could enter that room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 앞에서 놀라운 사실을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed at the start of a sentence to introduce a surprising fact.

phrases.en: The forest at night looks eerie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 기이하고 섬뜩하게 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the appearance looks weird and creepy.

explain_en: It has a creepier, more uncanny feel than '이상하다' and shows up more in writing and stories than in speech. It can also open a sentence, as in '괴이하게도', to introduce something surprising. In normal conversation '이상하다' or '수상하다' sounds more natural.
